rounds.title: Screening Round (MCQs)
rounds.qualification: Top 80% of all participants qualify for Round 2.
rounds.strictRule: Answers will NOT be accepted after the 30-second timer expires.

rounds.title: Core CS Concepts Round
rounds.strictRule: Answers will NOT be accepted after the 45-second timer expires.

rounds.title: Rapid Fire Round
rounds.qualification: Top 2 finalists qualify for the 1-on-1 Buzzer Grand Final.
rounds.strictRule: Each question must be answered within 3 seconds. After 3 seconds, the question is skipped automatically. Skipped or unanswered questions will NOT be repeated.

rounds.title: Buzzer Round (Grand Final)
rounds.qualification: Highest total score crowns the Champion of Battle of Brains 2026.
rounds.strictRule: Participants must press the buzzer after the question starts. The first buzzer gets the chance to answer. If a participant buzzes but cannot answer within 10 seconds, the turn passes. Premature or unnecessary buzzer pressing results in a warning or point deduction.

generalRules.title: Individual Participation Only
generalRules.description: Each participant competes as an individual (solo competitor). Group entries, pairs, or team collaborations are strictly not allowed.

generalRules.title: Mandatory Student Identification
generalRules.description: All participants must carry their original, valid University Student ID cards. Verification will take place at the reception registration desk.

generalRules.title: Prohibited Electronic Devices
generalRules.description: Mobile phones, smartwatches, programmable calculators, Bluetooth devices, and external notes are strictly prohibited inside the competition arena.

generalRules.title: Anti-Cheating & Integrity
generalRules.description: Cheating, prompting from the audience, unauthorized side discussions, or unfair means will lead to immediate and irreversible disqualification.

generalRules.title: Finality of Organizer Decisions
generalRules.description: The official jury and panel of judges' decisions regarding points, timing, buzzer logs, and disputes are final and binding on all participants.

generalRules.title: Punctuality & Reporting
generalRules.description: Participants must report to the competition venue at least 10 minutes before the scheduled start time. Late arrivals forfeit their slot without exception.

tieBreakerRules.title: Standard Tie-Breaker (2 Extra Questions)
tieBreakerRules.description: If two or more participants finish with equal scores in any qualifying round, 2 additional tie-breaker questions will be asked from each tied candidate.

tieBreakerRules.title: Decisive Sudden-Death Buzzer
tieBreakerRules.description: If participants remain tied after 2 additional questions, one decisive sudden-death buzzer question will be posed. The first candidate to buzz and answer correctly wins immediately.

tieBreakerRules.title: Buzzer Penalty in Sudden-Death
tieBreakerRules.description: If the first participant buzzes and answers incorrectly during sudden-death, the opposing tied candidate is automatically awarded the qualification slot.

disqualificationRules.description: Any participant found consulting a phone, wearable smart tech, internet search, or audience member will be disqualified instantly.
Disrespectful conduct, aggressive arguments with referees, or inappropriate language towards fellow participants will result in immediate eviction.

disqualificationRules.reason: Pressing the Buzzer Repeatedly without Reason
disqualificationRules.severity: Official Warning, Followed by Point Deductions & Disqualification
disqualificationRules.description: Frivolous, premature, or spam buzzer clicks intended to distract opponents or game the hardware will incur -1 point and potential disqualification.
Unreasonable stalls, refusal to answer within designated clock ticks, or disruptive stalling tactics will result in turn forfeiture.

questions.question: What is the worst-case time complexity of searching in a balanced Binary Search Tree (AVL Tree) with n nodes?
questions.explanation: A balanced BST maintains maximum height of O(log n), ensuring searches take at most O(log n) comparisons.

questions.question: In C++ or Java, which concept allows a subclass to provide a specific implementation of a method that is already provided by its superclass?
questions.explanation: Method Overriding occurs when a subclass defines a method with the exact same signature as a method in its parent class.

questions.question: Which normal form requires removing transitive dependencies of non-prime attributes on candidate keys?
questions.explanation: 3NF requires that the relation is in 2NF and no non-prime attribute is transitively dependent on any candidate key.

questions.question: At which layer of the OSI model does the Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) primarily operate to map IP to MAC addresses?
questions.explanation: ARP operates between Layer 2 (Data Link) and Layer 3 (Network) to resolve 32-bit IPv4 addresses into 48-bit physical MAC addresses.

questions.question: Which condition is NOT one of Coffman's four necessary conditions for a system deadlock to occur?
questions.explanation: For a deadlock to occur, resources must be non-preemptive (No Preemption). If preemption is allowed, deadlocks cannot form.

questions.question: In Agile Scrum framework, what is the recommended standard duration of a single Sprint cycle?
questions.explanation: Scrum guidelines dictate that a Sprint is a fixed-length event of one month or less (typically 2 weeks).

questions.question: Which informed search algorithm uses both path cost g(n) and heuristic estimate h(n) to find optimal path: f(n) = g(n) + h(n)?
questions.explanation: A* Search evaluates nodes by combining g(n) (cost so far) and h(n) (estimated cost to goal).

questions.question: Who formulated the famous Dining Philosophers problem to illustrate concurrency synchronization in 1965?
questions.explanation: Edsger W. Dijkstra originally formulated the dining philosophers problem as an exam question about synchronizing competing processes.
